TITLE: Palo Alto Networks Q1 FY27: beat, raise and a bet on AI
QUOTE: We beat guidance across every metric. … That momentum gives us confidence to materially raise our guidance for the year. Top-line strength also translated directly to the bottom line.
QUOTE_WHO: Nikesh Arora, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call, 18 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: Palo Alto Networks sells cybersecurity platforms for networks, security operations and identity, with nearly 70,000 network security customers. Network and AI security is two thirds of revenue. Fiscal 2027 revenue guide: USD 14.5bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue USD 3.44bn came 3.9% above the top of guidance; EPS USD 1.05 beat it by 7%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: Fiscal 2027 guide raised: revenue USD 14.52 to 14.57bn, +2.8% at midpoint; EPS USD 4.26 to 4.30.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: The USD 4.5bn Applied Compute deal costs up to 200bp of operating margin in fiscal 2028.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 81.3x forward earnings, 64% above the 2016 to 2026 average: the price has run ahead of earnings.

H_P1: AI-driven threats are turning into budgets
P1_PARAGRAPH: Revenue came 3.9% above the top of guidance and EPS 7.1% above, and the shares rose 6.4% on 19 November, the day after the release, on top of 9.9% the day before: surprise and reaction are aligned. AI-assisted attacks are turning into spending, with a record 170 customers consolidating. The case now runs on two engines: consolidation and a costly AI bet.
C1_TITLE: PANW: Q1 vs. guidance and fiscal 2027 guidance raise
C1_SUB: Q1 vs. top of company guidance · FY27 guidance midpoints vs. prior guidance · % (operating margin in percentage points) · Non-GAAP
C1_COMMENT: Every line beat, but the beat sits mainly in earnings rather than recurring revenue: EPS came 7.1% and operating margin 124bp above guidance, while next-generation security annualised recurring revenue (NGS ARR), came 1.8% above. The fiscal 2027 revenue raise, USD 395m at the midpoint, is three times the Q1 beat.
BASE_CASE: The investment case remains constructive: AI raises both the volume of attacks and the cost of fragmented defences, and Palo Alto is the main consolidator. We underwrite the fiscal 2027 guide of USD 4.26 to 4.30 of EPS and 26% to 27% revenue growth, with Applied Compute an option on secure enterprise AI, not a core driver. At 81.3x forward earnings the risk/reward is balanced: the multiple already pays for upgrades. Next test: recurring revenue vs. the USD 10.20 to 10.22bn fiscal Q2 guide.
UPSIDE: Recurring revenue above the USD 10.22bn top of the Q2 guide; operating margin held at 29.5% despite component costs; Applied Compute closing in fiscal Q3 2027 with early ARR visibility.
DOWNSIDE: Net-new platformizations back below 100 a quarter from 170 in Q1; gross margin, 75.2%, under 74% on SaaS mix and memory costs; deal dilution beyond the 200bp guided for fiscal 2028.
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Revenue rose 39% to USD 3.44bn, lifted by the CyberArk acquisition, now the Idira identity segment, and growth accelerated in all three segments. Network and AI security, two thirds of revenue, grew 20% to USD 2.3bn, with secure access service edge (SASE) ARR up 30% and software firewall ARR up 34%, a third consecutive acceleration. Cortex, the security operations platform, grew 53% (40% pro forma), with XSIAM ARR up over 65% to about USD 800m. Idira grew 23% pro forma and logged more than 100 cross-sell wins from the core base. Prisma AIRS, the AI security product, reached about USD 170m of ARR within five quarters, the fastest ramp in company history.

The reaction is aligned. EPS of USD 1.05 beat the top of the USD 0.96 to 0.98 guide by 7%, and the shares rose 6.4% on 19 November, the first session after the release, on top of 9.9% on 18 November, before the numbers; we read that gain as positioning into the print, not a confirmed driver. The confirmed drivers are the guidance raise and NGS ARR growth of 66%. The beat is of good quality: operating margin rose 50bp to 30.7% even as gross margin fell 170bp to 75.2% on component costs and SaaS mix, the main operational risk in analyst first takes.
H_A2: Outlook: guide raised, the AI deal adds cost
A2_PARAGRAPH: The fiscal 2027 guide, excluding Applied Compute, is now revenue USD 14.52 to 14.57bn (26% to 27% growth), NGS ARR USD 11.475 to 11.525bn, EPS USD 4.26 to 4.30, operating margin 29.5% and adjusted free cash flow margin 38%. The Q2 guide is revenue of USD 3.53 to 3.55bn and EPS of USD 1.01 to 1.03. Applied Compute, a USD 4.5bn all-stock deal with USD 100m of annualised revenue, should add USD 1bn of NGS ARR by fiscal 2029. The cost is up to 100bp of operating margin in fiscal 2027 and 200bp in fiscal 2028, plus under USD 3bn of capital spending through fiscal 2030.
H_C2: Valuation: the multiple ran ahead of earnings
C2_TITLE: PANW: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, January 2016 to 19 November 2026 · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus EPS · 40-week simple moving average · Log scale · Last price is the 19 November close, after the release
C2_COMMENT: The share price rose 76% over 12 months while 12m-forward consensus EPS rose 13%: the rerating, not earnings, did most of the work. At 81.3x, the forward P/E sits 64% above its 49.5x average since 2016, below the 97.1x peak of 9 October 2026 but well above the 63.1x one-year average. Since mid-August, before the previous results, EPS has risen 7% and the price has fallen 6%, so the derating has started. The price is 27% above its 40-week average. At an unchanged price, EPS would need to rise 29% to bring the multiple back to its one-year average.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, Palo Alto Networks fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call of 18 November 2026, AlphaSense, analyst research notes of 16 to 19 November 2026
